They reported that the peak electricity volume on the recent electricity bill was ridiculously high compared to the same period last year, but the production line schedule had not changed. I adjusted the usage data of the DEV-6020, and the situation is as follows: the meter clock deviates from the master station clock by 47 minutes, and the deviation has continued to increase over the past 9 days; The battery voltage inside the meter is 2.7V, which is below the 3.0V undervoltage warning threshold; The frozen daily data clock was moved forward overall, causing the daily electricity usage from 23:00 to 24:00 to be counted in the previous day's charge, exactly pushing it into the peak rate range; The 08:00 and 22:00 rate switching points are misaligned, and peak and off-peak electricity are linked together. Based on current data, the estimated monthly electricity rate deviation is about ±18,000 yuan. The table has been running for 9 years, with a rotation cycle of over 8 years.

Remote timing can only be temporarily corrected, battery undervoltage is irreversible. It is recommended to replace the meter on site and record frozen data. The degree of loss assessment is internally rated as "high" because the electricity in the rate segment cannot be precisely segmented day by day.

state: Internal email: Subject: Request for instructions on review of metering abnormality for {ticket} ({date}). Body: The collection success rate for customer {customer}'s meter was only 63% for 5 consecutive days recently (should be ≥98%), daily frozen electricity data was missing for 3 days, and the last valid data stopped at {date} 02:00. The system alarm was "communication interruption," but the on-site {device} heartbeat is normal, signal strength is -71dBm, and inspection found the SIM card online and the antenna not loose. Further comparison found that, from 2 hours before the interruption to during the interruption, the active power of this customer's upload data suddenly dropped from 12.3 kW to 0.2 kW, while during the same period the line loss rate of the adjacent distribution area rose from 4.8% to 5.1%, and the customer's instantaneous current was 0. According to the determination criteria: collection success rate <80% or continuous missing data ≥2 days is determined as collection communication interruption or data missing; if at the same time active power suddenly drops >90% and distribution area line loss rises, then bypass or short-circuiting of the metering circuit (electricity theft) is suspected. Currently both conditions are met: success rate 63%<80%, power drop (12.3-0.2)/12.3≈98.4%>90%, and line loss rose by 0.3 percentage points. According to the principle that "bypass takes priority over data supplementation," the final determination is bypass or short-circuiting of the metering circuit. Handling: on-site inspection is required, an on-site inspection form must be issued, and focus should be on checking the switch before the meter, secondary wiring, and meter box lead seals. Electricity loss estimate: based on 12.3 kW×16 hours/day×5 days≈984 kWh, the loss is obvious, and the confidence level is recorded as 2 points (relatively high). Attachment: the {order_no} spare parts requisition form has been archived, and no further reminder is needed.
